summary: Space-to-Cell nanobots using NASA satellite data to detect Witches' Broom disease in cassava crops early.
details: Our project introduces a "Space-to-Cell" precision agriculture system designed to protect Paraguay’s staple cassava crops (Manihot esculenta) from Witches' Broom disease (Ceratobasidium theobromae), a devastating fungal threat currently under phytosanitary alert. We integrate open satellite data from NASA ECOSTRESS, SMAP, and POWER as a macro-level radar to detect early thermal and water stress caused by vascular necrosis and to calculate the exact biological window when leaf stomata are fully open. Once a high-risk plot is pinpointed, farmers deploy biodegradable chemical nanobots (<50 nm) built with a chitosan-carbon chassis, disguised with sucrose to enter the phloem, propelled by glucose-oxidase enzymatic motors, and equipped with custom fungal antibodies and Quantum Dots. Upon binding to the hidden pathogen, the nanobot triggers a fluorescent signal calibrated using NASA Veggie optical spectroscopy protocols, enabling non-destructive, field-level diagnosis in just two hours before visible symptoms destroy the harvest.
